newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FORECAST-Israel October CPI seen up 0.7-0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Israel October CPI seen up 0.7-0.9 pct.

text.p: Israel's October consumer price index (CPI), due to be published on Friday, will show a rise of 0.7 to 0.9 percent, economists predicted on Thursday.
If inflation is 0.9 percent in October, the year-on-year inflation rate will be 11.2 percent.
Ptachia Bar Shavit, chief economist at Bank Hapoalim, said the bank was forecasting 0.9 percent, at the upper end of the range, because of higher housing and clothing prices.

Consumer prices have been rising 0.3-0.4 percent a month since July, after peaking at a 15 percent annualised rate in the first half of the year. But Bar Shavit said a higher October rate did not signal a resurgence of inflation.
"October is known to be a high month because of seasonal factors," he explained. These are mainly due to higher clothing prices in advance of the winter season.

Jonathan Katz, chief economist at Solid Capital Markets, said he was looking for a 0.8-0.9 percent CPI for the same reasons. "We had a series of devaluations of the shekel, close to two percent," he said. "That affects housing prices and imports."

Katz said if October inflation was in the expected range, the Bank of Israel would reduce short-term rates again at the end of this month. "My gut feeling is that (Governor Jacob) Frenkel will lower rates by his usual 0.3 percentage point, which is what he has been doing in the last few months," he said.

Economists cited the slowing economy as well as declining money supply growth as additional incentives for the bank to cut rates. M1 money supply has grown a nominal 10-12 percent this year, which Katz described as very low.
Expectations are that M1 will show a decline of as much as one percent for Octber, Katz added.
Hapoalim is expecting inflation to come down next year to about nine percent from a forecasted 11 percent for 1996.
